comments.author: spuz
comments.story: Tell HN: Toilet paper, hand sanitizer, and now web cams
comments.why: Gives a rundown of why laptop webcams lag behind.
comments.text: It's because the standard webcam interface is based on a slow USB 2 interface which can only support enough bandwidth for 720p video. To upgrade your webcam, laptop manufacturers would need to make significant changes to both the interface and the operating system. Add that onto the lack of economic incentive, it's just not worth the cost. Here's a good video that gives a run down: [VIDEO]

comments.author: Foivos
comments.story: Seven years later, I bought a new MacBook. For the first time, I don't love it
comments.why: Cited as background on laptop webcam limitations generally.
comments.text: A lot of it has to do with how laptop web cams work in general and it is not only Apple's problem [1]. A way to improve this situation a bit would be to be able to use the camera of an iPhone as a web cam, either over USB or wifi. You still have the compression and USB transfer, but at least you use the better optics of the phone. There are third party tools, such as EpocCam, that can do it, but require the installation of drivers. This should be a first party solution, in the same fashion as the "take photo" option from the right click menu on Mac OS, which uses an iPhone to take a photo and paste it directly on the open application of the computer.
